messages:
arjun: heads-up — seeing a recurring latency spike tied to on-demand bin switches between prefill and decode on ampere pools. spikes are short (20–40s) but add ~45–120ms tail for single-request p99. suspected kernel churn + KV warmup.
lee: ugh. any concrete traces or flamegraphs?
arjun: pasting the profiler snippet from the 2nd spike:
```
[2026-03-18 10:02:31] request id=abc123 slot=svc-ampere-7 kernel_pick=auto
[2026-03-18 10:02:31] selected_kernel: fused_prefill_v3
[2026-03-18 10:02:31] kv_cache_hit_rate: 12%
[2026-03-18 10:02:31] runtime_switch -> decode_path
[2026-03-18 10:02:31] fallback_kernel: decode_unfused_v1
[2026-03-18 10:02:32] token_latency_ms: 78
[2026-03-18 10:02:33] kv_warmup_evictions: 5
```
arjun: you can see pick -> fallback -> low KV hit -> higher per-token latency. pattern repeats as bining toggles.
olivia: interesting — same host saw a similar blip yesterday but we attributed to noisy neighbors. this looks deterministic under certain seq_len distributions.
lee: what's the seq_len distribution for those requests? short vs long?
arjun: mostly short (<=64) but with a 3–5% tail of 512+ which seems to trigger prefill-path decisions upstream. the router flips when it sees the occasional long ctx and then flips back, causing kernel + kv churn.
perf-bot: alert: recent deploy r13 bumped kernel selection confidence threshold from 0.6 -> 0.75 at 2026-03-17T22:14Z. correlated with first observed regressions.
olivia: that threshold change could make the selector more eager to pick fused_prefill for borderline cases, but the fallback to decode_unfused happens when we detect memory pressure on Ampere kernels.
sanjay: proposed quick mitigation: add hysteresis on path switching for 30s and bias kernel selection to prefer stable kernels for sessions with high short-ctx ratio. can we try a canary? :gear:
arjun: I ran a local canary where I forced prefill_kv_expiry to 10s -> reduced the p99 spike magnitude but didn't eliminate it. suspect multi-factor: kernel mismatch + KV warming + small batch sizes.
lee: do we have a repro harness? if not, we should create one that emits mixed seq_len traffic with same ratio and interarrival distribution.
qa-bot: creating job rn: harness-mixedseq-2026-03-18 (will run 2h canary against ampere pool). posting results in ~2h.
olivia: longer-term: we should teach autotuner to consider session stability (recent seq_len history) and prefer kernels that minimize fallback churn. also add a KV warmup prefetch for sessions that flip to prefill path.
sanjay: I'll open a ticket: INF-4123 — canary + hysteresis + autotune-signal enrichment. will include perf traces and the harness details.
arjun: thanks. immediate ask: can someone approve a 4h pin of kernel-selection-threshold on staging so QA can validate? small config flip.
lee: ack, approving now for staging. will monitor the canary run.
perf-bot: note: if we pin, metric 'kernel_switch_count' should drop; add an alert if it doesn't within 30m.
arjun: great — will follow up with updated logs once the canary finishes. :thumbsup:
